candidate.title: fCAB-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina fCAB-Seq schematic: O-ethylhydroxylamine (EtONH2) protection of 5-formylcytosine in genomic DNA, paired with an EtONH2-untreated control, followed by separate bisulfite treatment and PCR amplification. The five-position cartoons explain base encoding, not a literal genomic sequence. The left 5fC-residue icon is explanatory; the right DNA icon denotes DNA products without specifying adapters or physical pooling. fCAB-seq is the capitalization alias used in the sources. fC-Seal, ChIP-fCAB-Seq, RNA adaptations and fC-CET are not additional targets of this schematic.

states.label: Genomic DNA represented by C / 5mC / 5hmC / 5fC / 5caC
features: Illustrated positions, from left to right: unmodified cytosine, 5-methylcytosine, 5-hydroxymethylcytosine, 5-formylcytosine and 5-carboxylcytosine.
The two routes represent matched DNA from the same sample; the control receives no EtONH2 protection.
Colored side-group icons distinguish cytosine modifications; no terminal chemistry, adapter, barcode, attachment or compartment is specified.

Center: upper Control route and lower O-ethylhydroxylamine (EtONH2) route; lower 5fC position labeled Blocked

evidence.quote: fCAB-seq is a method for EtONH2-modified bisulfite sequencing for base-resolution detection of 5fC in genomic DNA.
Through comparison of EtONH2-treated bisulfite sequencing and traditional bisulfite sequencing of the same sample, we can determine the genomic locations of 5fC at single-base level (Figure 6A).

states.label: EtONH2-treated DNA with blocked 5fC
features: The lower branch marks the original 5fC position as Blocked.
The other four positions remain depicted as C, 5mC, 5hmC and 5caC; the protected 5fC is retained in its DNA sequence context.
Protection concerns susceptibility to subsequent bisulfite-mediated deamination; the generic blocking icon does not specify a chemical structure.

states.label: Control bisulfite/PCR DNA: T-C-C-T-T
features: In the cartoon order, original C, 5fC and 5caC give T; original 5mC and 5hmC give C.

The final generic DNA label is represented here as a branch-specific product; the arrows do not establish mixing with the treated product.

operations.label: O-ethylhydroxylamine (EtONH2)
operations.description: On the treatment route, modify DNA-bound 5fC to the blocked form shown in the lower cartoon. The other route remains an EtONH2-untreated control.
operations.mechanism: EtONH2-based protection prevents 5fC from bisulfite-mediated deamination in the subsequent step. The figure does not resolve the blocking group structure.
operations.information_effect: The original 5fC position remains associated with its genomic DNA context and acquires different conversion behavior from unprotected 5fC.

operations.label: Bisulfite treatment / PCR amplification
operations.description: Process the upper Control route separately. The original five-position C/5mC/5hmC/5fC/5caC substrate becomes the depicted T-C-C-T-T DNA product. The two named actions remain a combined schematic block.
operations.mechanism: The paper identifies unprotected 5fC conversion to uracil during bisulfite sequencing; after the depicted PCR step its position is represented as T. The figure also depicts unmodified C and 5caC as T and 5mC and 5hmC as C.
operations.information_effect: Provides the matched conventional-bisulfite reference. A T at the illustrated original 5fC position is not unique to 5fC; 5mC and 5hmC are both represented as C and are not separated by this branch.

operations.label: Bisulfite treatment / PCR amplification
operations.description: Process the lower EtONH2-protected route separately. The blocked five-position DNA becomes the depicted T-C-C-C-T DNA product, retaining C specifically at the original 5fC position relative to the control cartoon.
operations.mechanism: Prior EtONH2 protection makes 5fC resist bisulfite-mediated deamination, so the amplified sequence represents it as C. Original C and 5caC are depicted as T, and 5mC and 5hmC as C.
operations.information_effect: The readout carrier is amplified DNA sequence. At corresponding genomic positions, additional C retention in the EtONH2-treated sample relative to the conventional-bisulfite control supports base-resolution 5fC detection. Treated C alone also includes 5mC/5hmC signal and does not uniquely identify 5fC. The diagram depicts ideal base outcomes, not a guarantee of complete conversion or quantitative accuracy. Sequencing and between-branch comparison are reported by the paper but are not drawn as local operations here.
